types.description: A repository as cloned and parsed locally
A package, app or library inside the repository (a Python package or a monorepo workspace).
An external package the code depends on (from manifests and imports).
A class (or interface, struct or type declaration) with its full source.
A function or method with its full source and graph metrics
Lines outside any function or class (module-level code, configuration, other text), so every line of every stored file is in the graph.
One heading section of a markdown file in the repository (README, docs, ADRs, changelog).
One rule from a CODEOWNERS file.
A commit from the local clone
A commit author identity (name and email)
A branch in the local clone.
How one commit changed one file, with the changed line ranges.
A GitHub organisation that owns repositories.
A pull request: the unit that ties a change to its discussion, review, checks and the code it touched.
One file changed by a pull request
A review submitted on a pull request.
A comment on a specific line of a pull request diff
An issue (bug report, feature request or discussion) in a repository.
A conversation comment on an issue or on a pull request (not tied to a diff line).
A label used on issues and pull requests.
A milestone grouping issues and pull requests.
A published release of the repository.
A branch on GitHub, including branches opened by the Actron build step on the fork.
One check (for example a test job) reported on a commit
Represents a user in the Linear workspace, including personal details, role, and activity status.
Represents a team within the Linear workspace used for organizing issues and workflows.
Represents a task or issue in Linear, which can be assigned, prioritized, and tracked through workflow states.
Represents a workflow state (e.g., Todo, In Progress, Done) within a team’s issue lifecycle.
Represents a tag or label used to categorize issues within a team, including color and grouping.
Represents a project in Linear used to group related issues and track progress toward goals.
Represents a comment made on an issue in Linear, supporting markdown and threaded replies.
Represents an inbox notification for a user, such as mentions, assignments, or status changes.
Represents a saved filtered view of issues created by a user, allowing customized issue filtering and display.
One account of a person in one tool, and how it was matched.
A group of people (from a Linear team or a Slack user group).
A reference found in text (ENG-17, #123, a URL, a path, a symbol)
A named behaviour of the product (for example 'report export'), linked to the code that implements it and the text that discusses it.
A statement of how the software should or should not behave, with its exact source quote
How changes are usually made in an area of the code: test command, files that change together, review norms
A feature request, bug report or question raised through Slack or the UI
What the investigator agent found for a request: the evidence it handed to the builder.
One run of the coding agent for an approved request.
